summary: Iter 77 — Backhaul Hunter AI, driver assignment, driver CRUD, PDF docs with driver embedded, and daily-cap regression. 19/19 pytest cases pass; frontend Desk/Backhaul/Drivers tabs all render and CRUD works end-to-end.

issues: Console hydration warning: `<span>` cannot be child of `<option>` — comes from the preview editor's static instrumentation wrapper around the option children (`{c.name} ({c.mc_number})`). Real source is fine; only a runtime warning caused by the emergent x-* wrapper. Non-blocking but visible in devtools.

critical_code_review_comments: Backhaul hunter code path verified by reading source: `_open_hunt` fires when outbound load reaches 'delivered' & driver.home_base city != dest city, dedupes by outbound_load_id; `_process_hunts` books after ≥2 scans w/ score≥70, OR score≥88 immediately, OR ≥9 min forced; BH- load carries the same driver+carrier and dest=driver.home_base. Completion path closes the hunt via `booked_load_id` match. All expected.
`stats.sourced_today` correctly filters `load_type != 'backhaul'` in both `run_cycle` and `/status` — confirmed by tests (15/15 remains 15/15).
PDF builders (`_ratecon_pdf`, `_bol_pdf`, `_pod_pdf`) embed driver name+CDL rows. Verified by PyMuPDF text extraction on live ratecon.pdf that driver 'Darnell Griggs' is present.
`/broker-autopilot/loads/{id}/docs/{doc}.pdf` returns 400 with stage-name in detail before the doc is available (STAGES index gate); returns 200 at/past correct stage. Verified.
`_ensure_drivers` is idempotent (skips carriers that already have drivers). Called from `run_cycle` and `list_drivers` — safe.
`_pick_driver` sorts by last_assigned_at asc → round-robins across drivers within a carrier. Good.
MINOR: `edit_driver` accepts empty `is_active=None` but doesn't validate at least one truthy field — currently returns 400 only when whole payload is None-only. Not a blocker.

MINOR: In `DriverRoster.jsx` line 54, `<option>{c.name} ({c.mc_number})</option>` — under the preview editor's static instrumentation this triggers a `<span> inside <option>` hydration warning. Consider wrapping the label in a template string to keep it purely textual (e.g. `{`${c.name} (${c.mc_number})`}` on one expression) if the warning bothers you; production build is unaffected.
